extracted.intended_audience: art historians, students, and readers of Renaissance painting biographies
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative standards and quality criteria used in Vasari's Lives for judging Renaissance Italian paintings (technique, composition, colour, iconography, invention, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelikeness of heads/facial expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads and faces should be lifelike and possess beautiful, very lifelike heads (e.g., 'the most beautiful and most lifelike heads that Stefano ever made').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular praise is given when heads are of the size of life and show natural, expressive countenances; this is a marker of superior portraiture and figure-painting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness and durability of colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: The colouring should remain beautiful and fresh over time (e.g., 'the colouring of the whole work, having been executed with diligence, has remained beautiful even to our own day').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durability is linked to technique (proper fresco execution) and diligence; exposure to weather can damage colours but careful original execution preserves them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct fresco technique (avoid retouching on dry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works executed in fresco should be painted with diligence on the wet plaster rather than retouched on the dry ('Stefano did not retouch it on the dry, but used diligence in executing it well in fresco').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper fresco technique leads to long-lasting colour; retouching on dry is implied to be inferior and to reduce longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gracefulness and expressive countenance of angels
rubrics_metrics.description: Angels should be made 'most gracious in countenance and very beautiful in expression' and often depicted with specific visual conventions (e.g., garments ending in clouds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expression and grace in angelic figures are repeatedly praised as a hallmark of a master's style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconographic clarity and purposeful composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and groupings should clearly convey their theological or symbolic function (e.g., prophets supporting the Church 'to show that both of them defend Holy Church from heretics with their learning').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition should serve narrative or doctrinal clarity, using positioning and gestures to communicate meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive motifs / artist's hallmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated motifs or emblems (e.g., the peacock as 'almost the hall-mark of pictures executed by him') are an identifying strength of an artist's oeuvre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recognizable personal emblem or recurrent motif can be a mark of authorship and stylistic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Richness and narrative detail in predellas and small-scale scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Predellas and small scenes should be filled with narrative detail (e.g., 'filled the predella with scenes in little figures from the life of that Saint').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to many small narrative vignettes demonstrates care, inventiveness, and mastery of figural miniaturization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and organization of large narrative cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale wall cycles should be thoughtfully distributed and composed around the room (e.g., Aldigieri 'distributing one scene over the walls of that hall on every side, with a single ornament encircling it right round').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful large narratives show coherent arrangement, ornamental framing, and considered sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical accuracy and attention to relevant detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Depictions of historical or martial subjects should show intelligence and judgment by taking into consideration relevant details ('took into consideration all the things that can be taken into consideration in a serious war').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate costumery, tactics, and contextual detail increase the work's authority and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness and conception in complex/theological subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Works on complex or apocalyptic themes should demonstrate 'beautiful conceptions' and imaginative invention (e.g., Paradise with many choirs of angels; Last Judgment scenes with angels and demons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original visual inventions and imaginative detail in theological scenes are praised and influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and effectiveness in moral allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Personifications (virtues, vices) and moral exemplars should be clearly represented, tracking celebrated virtuous figures versus those fallen into misery or Hell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear allegorical representation (virtues/vices, moral outcomes) is a measure of narrative and didactic success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and workmanship/labor invested
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of labour and diligence invested in a work is a quality marker ('carried out so well and with such great diligence...'), often correlated with superior results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex compositions, many figures, and careful finishing are repeatedly noted as signs of a practised master.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of perspective and landscape depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspective and receding landscapes should be handled convincingly (e.g., 'a very beautiful view in perspective of a landscape receding into the distance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful integration of architectural and landscape perspective is repeatedly singled out for praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity, variety of figures, and foreshortening skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Large compositions with many figures, diverse attitudes, nudity, and skilful foreshortenings are valued ('more than three hundred figures... many foreshortenings').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variety of pose, anatomical daring (nudes), and foreshortening demonstrate technical virtuosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour harmony and charm
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall colouring that is 'very charming and beautiful' is an important aesthetic criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour harmonies that enhance composition and expressiveness are a recurring standard of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait realism and vivacity from life
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits painted 'from the life' that appear 'absolutely alive' are highly prized (e.g., portrait 'can challenge comparison with any...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lifelike portraiture, likeness, and vivacity count strongly toward a painter's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalism and accurate depiction of varied peoples/costumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeiting things of nature—figures, distant landscapes, and people of diverse nations and costumes—is praised (e.g., depiction of Turks, Greeks, and diverse faces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistic representation of different types and costumes, and careful observational detail, strengthen a composition's verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering of materials and reflected light
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical rendering of material qualities (splendour of armour, reflected lights) is a mark of knowledge and skill ('knowledge of Luca ... in the splendour of his armour and in the reflected lights').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to light effects and material surfaces increases realism and technical esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical accuracy and vivacity of nudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nudes should be made convincingly alive and anatomically true ('showed the true method of making nudes... to appear alive').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful nudity requires study of anatomy and composition, and is singled out as a major technical achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation/restoration caution for masterpieces
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be better to leave works 'half spoilt' when they were made by men of excellence rather than have them retouched by inferior masters (warning about restoration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration by lesser hands can harm a master's work; careful conservation ethics are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive influence and contribution to later artists
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovations (angels, demons, divisions of the Heavens, inventions) that encourage and ease later artists' work are a mark of an important master ('he encouraged all those who have lived after him').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An artist's value includes their influence and the degree to which later masters borrow or learn from their inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of portraiture/self-portraiture as compositional device
rubrics_metrics.description: Including portraits of patrons, contemporaries, or self-portraits within larger works is noted and valued (Luca 'portrayed himself and many of his friends').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inserting identifiable figures can serve commemorative, social, or documentary functions and is regarded positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice and mastery of medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and control of medium (fresco, oil, distemper, stucco) matter for the quality and effect of the work (examples: panels in distemper, fresco cycles, stucco work praised as 'so beautiful and so ornate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastery in multiple media and appropriate medium choice for subject/location are valued.
